decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet shelf display is a core variant of the firm's display catalogue, uses existing production capacity at low marginal cost, and shows no evidence of falling short of aspirations.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a modest extension of the core offer for hanging goods, and a large firm's slack allows it to stay in the catalogue without triggering problemistic search.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format for brand and retail customers and sits squarely within the established business, so dropping it is unlikely.
The eighth-pallet display completes the standard pallet-format range retailers expect, and keeping it costs little relative to the firm's one-stop positioning.
The wooden display pallet departs from the paper-based core and its results are more uncertain, but available slack and its sustainability appeal justify keeping it for now.

Demand for displays of physical media is likely shrinking and may fall below aspirations, but the product shares the quarter-pallet platform and can be repurposed, so it is kept for now while under review.
